charm-species-demon.allpeater.name: Selector Ring of Parted Volleys
charm-species-demon.allpeater.flavor: Filed from a spent barrel-collar and notched around the rim, so a thumb can find each setting in the dark. Turn it and every muzzle on the field hears the click: bore deep into a throat, or spread the shot across the rows.

charm-species-demon.allpeater.name: Trilane Selector Collar
charm-species-demon.allpeater.flavor: Filed from a barrel collar that burst its own liner, re-bored, and notched with a detent for every lane the gunner works. The thumb finds its setting in the dark, and the standing ward answers the same click the muzzles do — draining off the lane gone quiet, banking under the lane taking fire. Cover is allocated the way shot is: never everywhere, always somewhere.

charm-species-demon.ashthreepeater.name: The Trifurcate Clinker
charm-species-demon.ashthreepeater.flavor: Its throats burned through and fused into a knuckle of clinker, the bores still open, still warm against the thumb. Press it to a marching order and the ash rides out with it: nothing it touches burns halfway, and nothing it finishes ever comes back green.

charm-species-demon.ashthreepeater.name: Clinker of the Trine Bores
charm-species-demon.ashthreepeater.flavor: Its trifurcate throats burned through and slumped into a knuckle of clinker, the bores still open, nothing left inside to spit. What is already wholly burnt cannot burn again. Press it to a marching order and the ash rides out with it, laying that same char crust over every deployed thing; break the crust and it stays broken, for ash does not grow back.

charm-species-demon.bucketnutzombie.name: The Split Headstone
charm-species-demon.bucketnutzombie.flavor: A wedge of grave-marker, split from the inside and banded with strips of hammered pail-iron. The dead never turn their heads aside, so whatever stands in the way is simply gone through.

charm-species-demon.bucketnutzombie.name: Rim of the Hammered Pail
charm-species-demon.bucketnutzombie.flavor: A hoop cut from the lip of a battered pail, beaten flat and folded back on itself until the metal rings dull. Iron learns hardness the way a dead skull learns it — one blow at a time, taken square, and every dent kept for good.
